definitions.explanation: Describes an abundant harvest or the state of being rich and productive. Used literally for agricultural abundance and figuratively for cultural or creative richness.

examples.japanese: {豊穣|ほうじょう}の{秋|あき}を{祝|いわ}う。
examples.english: To celebrate an abundant autumn harvest.

examples.japanese: {豊穣|ほうじょう}な{大地|だいち}がこの{地域|ちいき}の{誇|ほこ}りだ。
examples.english: The fertile land is the pride of this region.

examples.japanese: {村|むら}の{人|ひと}たちは{毎年|まいとし}、{五穀豊穣|ごこくほうじょう}を{祈|いの}る{祭|まつ}りを{行|おこな}う。
examples.english: The villagers hold a festival every year to pray for an abundant grain harvest.

notes: A literary, somewhat elevated word. The compound {五穀豊穣|ごこくほうじょう} (abundant harvest of the five grains) is a very common set phrase used in Shinto prayers and harvest festivals. The five grains traditionally refer to {米|こめ} (rice), {麦|むぎ} (wheat/barley), {粟|あわ} (millet), {豆|まめ} (beans), and {黍|きび} (proso millet). Also used figuratively: {豊穣|ほうじょう}な{文化|ぶんか} (rich culture), {豊穣|ほうじょう}な{想像力|そうぞうりょく} (rich imagination).
